clue.text: Game spirit shown after a dance

indicators.note: the spirit is placed after the dance in the answer

parts.note: to hop is to dance, and a hop is an informal dance
Scotch is whisky, a spirit

explanation.surface: Drinks come out after the ceilidh, a party spirit following the dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown after' puts the spirit second. HOPSCOTCH is the children's game of hopping through chalked squares.
explanation.definitionFit: A playground pastime of hopping between numbered chalk squares, so it is a children's game.

clue.text: Compensation for unsatisfactory plant

parts.note: off means not up to standard, as with food gone off
to set is to plant, as seedlings are set out

explanation.surface: Damages paid out for a faulty factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory but is a verb. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that counterbalances a loss, so an amount set against it.

clue.text: Self-conscious about blunder, so drink

indicators.note: the first piece goes about the second, around it

parts.note: shy means self-conscious
to err is to blunder

explanation.surface: Embarrassed about a gaffe, someone reaches for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ERR inside SHY. 'so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified Spanish wine, so an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: An innkeeper offered this guy stable employment

definitions.text: An innkeeper offered this guy stable employment

parts.words: An innkeeper offered this guy stable employment
parts.note: stable reads as secure, but means a job in the stables looking after travellers' horses at an inn

explanation.definitionFit: A man who looked after guests' horses at an inn, a stableman.

clue.text: Cowherd getting in a stew

indicators.note: in a stew means flustered and mixed up, so the letters of cowherd are rearranged

explanation.surface: A farmhand gets flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a stew' rearranges COWHERD, and the result is itself a kind of stew, so the whole clue defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick soup or stew, often of seafood, so something to cook in a pot.

clue.text: A gang, one old coppers would find vicious

parts.note: a band is a gang
taken as written
D was the symbol for pennies, the copper coins of pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: A gang is something the police once found brutal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' looks like police, but means copper coins: d stood for the old penny before Britain went decimal in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned means depraved or wholly given up to vice, so wicked.

clue.text: Willing sufferer the scholar-to his cost maybe

parts.note: an MA, a Master of Arts, is a scholar

indicators.note: maybe suggests a different possible order for the words his cost

explanation.surface: A scholar who suffers gladly, to his own cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' makes SOCHIST from HIS COST. 'the' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes pleasure in their own pain, so one who suffers willingly.

clue.text: Fed-up over closure, putting up some resistance

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second
in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
an ending is a closure

explanation.surface: Sick of a closure, protesters are resisting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FED into DEF, which 'over' sets above ENDING.
explanation.definitionFit: Defending means guarding or holding out against attack, offering resistance.

clue.text: Dedicated man arranging outside broadcast at the last minute

parts.note: late means at the last minute, almost too late

explanation.surface: A devoted producer sets up a broadcast from location with no time to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranging' is only a link here. An oblate is a layperson dedicated to a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: A layperson who has dedicated their life to a monastic community, so a religiously devoted person.

clue.text: Lovemaking complaint

definitions.meaning: fondness and tender attachment, the feeling behind courtship
an old medical sense: a disease or ailment of a part of the body

explanation.definitionFit: The word means tender fondness and also, in older medical language, a disorder or ailment.

clue.text: Points to the centre once more

parts.note: E and N are two compass points, east and north
the core is the centre of something

explanation.surface: A speaker keeps steering the discussion back to the central issue again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is only a link. The definition is the call of an audience for a repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience's call meaning 'again', asking a performer to repeat or continue.

clue.text: Favours a county fencing in the finer ruins

indicators.note: the county's letters surround the other piece like a fence

parts.note: BEDS is the abbreviation for Bedfordshire, an English county

indicators.note: ruins tells us the word finer is wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A county council grants privileges to a landowner who has fenced off some old ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruins' makes FRIEN from FINER; 'fencing in' puts that inside BEDS. BEDS is short for Bedfordshire, a county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: To befriend someone is to help or support them, close in sense to favouring them.

clue.text: The business woman had made use of a club

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
she is the pronoun for a woman
'd is the short form of had, as in she'd

explanation.surface: A businesswoman once used her membership of an exclusive club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' looks like a society to join, but it is a cudgel. A cosh is a short heavy weapon; 'The' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosh someone is to strike them with a short heavy bludgeon, a kind of club.

clue.text: No longer a habit to regret

definitions.text: No longer a habit to regret

parts.words: No longer a habit to regret
parts.note: a habit here is clothing, as a monk's robe; the coarse garment once worn as a sign of penitence is rarely seen now

explanation.definitionFit: Coarse fabric worn, with ashes, as an outward show of repentance in former times.

clue.text: Many captivated by fearsome heights will get guides

indicators.note: the first piece is held captive inside the other two

parts.note: dire means dreadful or fearsome
tors are rocky hilltops, as on Dartmoor
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

explanation.surface: Many climbers are thrilled by frightening peaks and will hire mountain guides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captivated by' puts C inside DIRE TORS. A tor is a rocky outcrop on a hilltop in the English West Country.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who direct people or projects lead and steer them, as guides do.

clue.text: The promptitude of an aristocrat in letter writing

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman, an aristocrat
the letter S written out in full as a word is ess

explanation.surface: A nobleman shows admirable punctuality in answering his correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is only a link. The letter is S spelt out as a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Promptitude is being early or prompt, so the quality of being ahead of time.

clue.text: Aim to cause trouble

definitions.meaning: to attempt or strive for something
to vex or annoy, as in testing someone's patience

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to make an attempt at something and to tax or irritate a person.

clue.text: Several are in contention

indicators.note: the letters wanted sit within the following word

explanation.surface: Quite a few teams remain in the running for the title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are in' signals letters inside 'contention'.
explanation.definitionFit: A modest but definite number, so it can stand for several.

clue.text: The old-fashioned bearing tree

parts.note: ye is an archaic way of writing the, as in Ye Olde Shoppe
W, west, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned fruit tree still bearing its crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' looks like fruiting, but it is a compass direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark evergreen conifer often grown in churchyards, so a tree.

clue.text: Encourage a friend content in retirement

indicators.note: the piece becomes the contents of a friend, held inside

parts.note: a mate is a friend

indicators.note: in retirement means going backwards, so the word in is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Cheer up a pal who is happy now that he has retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' turns IN into NI and 'content' sets NI inside A MATE. 'content' looks like 'happy' but means contents.
explanation.definitionFit: To animate is to enliven or spur on, close in sense to encouraging.

clue.text: Mere anomalous issue, he wrote

indicators.note: anomalous means irregular, so the word mere is put out of order

parts.note: issue means offspring, so a son

explanation.surface: An odd little publication that one writer produced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anomalous' makes EMER from MERE. Ralph Waldo Emerson was the American essayist and poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was a nineteenth-century American essayist and poet, a writer.

clue.text: Some people like to be alone with a good novel

indicators.note: some marks a part of the words that follow, letters lifted from inside

explanation.surface: Some people like nothing better than solitude and a good book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' points to part of 'alone with'; 'people like to be' and 'a good' are padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Novel as an adjective means original or fresh, never seen before.

clue.text: A person could come to some harm by the look of it

definitions.text: A person could come to some harm by the look of it

parts.words: A person could come to some harm by the look of it
parts.note: a malicious glance believed to cast a curse, so harm comes literally from a look

explanation.definitionFit: A gaze superstitiously thought to bring bad luck or injury to whoever receives it.

clue.text: Announces the end in ringing tones

definitions.text: Announces the end in ringing tones

parts.words: Announces the end in ringing tones
parts.note: a bell tolling for a death or the end of something, read as a person speaking loudly

explanation.definitionFit: A tolled bell signals a death or a finish, so it announces an ending with its sound.

clue.text: Smoother and quietly superior little beasts

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
U means upper-class or superior
mice are small animals

explanation.surface: Gentle, quietly snobbish small creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoother' looks like a comparative adjective, but it is a thing that smooths: a light volcanic stone for scrubbing skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A light porous volcanic stone used to scrub away hard skin, so it smooths things.

clue.text: Greek character admitting a casual shirt means a bad mark

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: sigma is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a T-shirt is a casual shirt, giving T

explanation.surface: A Greek man who turns up in a casual shirt is frowned upon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' puts T inside SIGMA. 'means' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace or shame attached to someone.

clue.text: Possibly those over 50 will get basic accommodation

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second
possibly signals that the word those may be rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: People over fifty may be stuck with plain lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' makes HOSTE from THOSE; 'over' sets it above L.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap shared lodging for travellers or students, plain and simple accommodation.

clue.text: Place where no-one tense is backed

indicators.note: backed means the run of pieces is read from end to start

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
taut means tense or tight

explanation.surface: A place where nobody nervous is supported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns NO + I + TAUT + IS into SI TUAT I ON. 'where' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation is a location or site, the place where something is.

clue.text: Delayed by conservationists lying concealed

parts.note: late means delayed
NT is the National Trust, a British conservation charity

explanation.surface: Environmentalists were late to spot something hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is the British charity that preserves historic houses and land. 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Latent describes something present but dormant or not yet visible, so hidden.

clue.text: Protective covering for tree doing badly

indicators.note: badly tells us the words tree doing are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A protective wrap for a tree that is not thriving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges TREE DOING. A redingote is a long double-breasted coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A long coat, originally a riding coat, worn to keep off the weather.

clue.text: A flighty creature's childish 10 across

definitions.meaning: a creature of flight, a songbird
10 across is read as complaint, so a fungal infection common in babies

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a speckled songbird and also a yeast infection common in infants' mouths.

clue.text: May take a cut, being at all times in the black

indicators.note: the first piece sits within the colour

parts.note: sable is black in heraldry
ever means always, at all times

explanation.surface: A business that may face cuts despite always being profitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the black' looks like 'in profit', but the black is SABLE, which holds EVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Severable means able to be separated or cut off.
